items.text: Keycloak rolling out in your own namespace, with the two timestamps that show how long it took.
The registry refusing an unapproved image, with the not on the whitelist message.
The discovery document, showing the token endpoint, the JWKS URI, and S256 support.
Your client's configuration: public, standard flow only, one exact redirect URI, PKCE required.
A decoded access token showing customer_id and aud: shopfront-api, and the mappers that put them there.
The three PKCE refusals: wrong verifier, replayed code, password grant.
The injected search returning card numbers, and the Semgrep finding that names the line.
The three XSS contexts in one page, before and after.
Alice's valid token reading order 1002 with a 200, and the same request answering 404 after the fix.
alg: none and a tampered payload both refused.
The test run that was red before the fix and green after it, with the count in both.
Two pull requests on the lab Git server: the service with its tests, and your Day 16 log.
The two quota refusals, with the full message, and the ClusterIP Service that was allowed.
The chart version and the two --set overrides you installed Kong with, and the four ClusterIP Services it created.
A 200 through the gateway showing Via: 1.1 kong and both Kong latency headers.
Both CORS preflight answers, showing that the disallowed origin still got a 200.
The rate limit going from 200 to 429, with the Retry-After header.
Four token answers: no token, good, tampered signature, expired, and what changed when you removed claims_to_verify.
The Gateway at Programmed=Unknown / Waiting for controller, and the same command after the annotations.
Your ninety/ten count out of sixty requests, and the count again after setting the weight to zero.
The blue/green switch and its rollback, and the twenty 200s during the broken rollout with rollout status exiting 1.
The netpolicy eval answers: false, false with the ingress rule, true with the egress rule, and the one-line list.
A merged learning log entry for Day 17.
A pod's logs read with kubectl logs, then NotFound after you deleted the pod.
kubectl top nodes answering error: Metrics API not available, and an empty metrics.k8s.io API group.
A container's own memory use read out of /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current.
The collector's Service showing two ports instead of six, and one receiver in its rendered config.
HTTP 200 from /v1/logs and /v1/traces, and the collector's debug exporter counting one record and one span.
Loki's label list (one label, service_name) and your own log line fetched back by query_range.
A trace fetched from Tempo by its ID, and the Loki PVC at 1Gi rather than the chart's 10Gi.
The Tempo datasource health check failing on port 3100, and passing after you fixed the values file.
Kubernetes Events queryable in Loki as {service_name="k8s-events"}, and the collector's ClusterRole limited to events.
Zero events recording the Secret you read, and /logs answering NotFound.
The test notification showing an empty severity in its title, and the real notification showing severity: critical and "QUERY":2.
The rule going inactive to firing to a resolved notification, and an empty namespace at the end.
The inherited account: three ports open to 0.0.0.0/0 and two buckets with nothing switched on.
A Prowler run with your five agreed checks, eight failures, and prowler exit 3.
One finding's framework mapping, and the count of frameworks it carries (36).
The PCI DSS 4.0 requirement text for 1.3.1, read from the tool.
gate.sh failing with five blocking findings, and the reason it exits 2 rather than 0 when the report is missing.
custodian validate passing, and a dry run's resources.json holding exactly one security group.
Port 22 gone, port 3389 tagged c7n-close-me with a date, and port 443 untouched.
The stale cache reporting count:1 on a deleted rule, and count:0 with --cache-period 0.
The gate going green only after an exception with a reason, an owner and a review date.
Two events published to the bus and exactly one delivered to the queue.
runbook.sh printing CHECK, CHANGE and CONFIRM, and exiting 0 on the confirm step.
The platform's healthz over verified TLS with no -k, and two identical 401s.
A finding id you were not given answering 404, and your own answering 200.
A token's ping showing your scopes, and a review call that finds a secret and stores nothing.
A merged learning log entry for Day 19.
capstone/gate.sh running all seven gates, and the first run answering RELEASE GATE: BLOCKED on your own clean tree.
Gitleaks naming three rules on a committed token, and still refusing after the file was deleted in a later commit.
The registry's 403 ... Reason: blocked by rule event-stream, from both npm install and the gate's npm ci.
Semgrep's capstone.policy.exec-taint finding, marked Blocking, on the line where a query parameter reached exec().
Conftest refusing an unpinned :latest base and USER root, with 3 tests, 1 passed, 2 failures.
Checkov's CKV_AWS_24 and CKV_AWS_23 on the bastion security group, and ten passing checks on the good one.
Kyverno's pass: 2, fail: 2, and the cluster's own violates PodSecurity "baseline:latest" Event after kubectl said created.
RELEASE GATE: PASS with EX-001 in place, and both gates refusing again once the expiry date was in the past.
A merge attempt answering HTTP 405 with a secret on the branch, and HTTP 200 once it was gone.
Ten 200 answers during a broken rollout, rollout status exiting 1, and the reason only in kubectl get events.
The rollback naming the previous digest, and the pods' imageID proving which bytes are serving.
docs/capstone/evidence.md on main, with a "Not covered" section you wrote honestly.
